# Protecting Your Bank Account in the Age of AI


Share:


- Copied!


-
-
-


Artificial intelligence is becoming increasingly common in everyday activities. Generating shopping lists, organizing budgets and planning vacations have never been easier. But as AI tools become more capable, it’s important to know where to draw the line between convenience and security.


### Keep Your Banking Credentials Private


No matter how much technology changes, the golden rule of banking remains the same: **Never share your digital banking credentials, passwords, or passcodes with any unauthorized third party, including AI tools or assistants.**


Do not allow AI tools, assistants or agents to:


- Access your account through oldnational.com or the ONB mobile app
- Change account, payment or security settings
- Make payments or transfers


The reasoning is simple: You should remain in control. Sharing sensitive information with third parties puts your account and personal information at risk, and is the most consistently dangerous fraud tactic affecting millions of consumers each year. Fortunately, keeping your credentials private is easy with the right tools.


### Account Alerts: Stay in the Know


One of the best ways to maintain control over your account is to set up account alerts. Alerts are easily customizable and can help you stay informed about your account activity, so you can act quickly if something seems off. You can set up phone or email alerts in Old National Digital Banking.


### How to Set Up Account Alerts in Old National Digital Banking


**On desktop** : Navigate to **Notifications** in the top navigation and set up the account alerts you want.


**In the ONB mobile app:** Tap the **Settings** gear in the top right, then select **Push Notifications** to customize your alerts. Make sure push notifications are also enabled in your device settings.


### Business Banking Users: Review Your Account Access


Because business banking accounts may have multiple authorized users, monitoring account access is especially important. It's a good idea for primary administrators to periodically review who has access to their accounts, and the specific permissions assigned to each user.


To review user permissions, log into business digital banking and select **Manage Users.** Here, you can add and remove users, grant permissions, and modify account access.[Check out our business digital banking guides to learn more.](https://www.oldnational.com/business/small-business-banking/services/digital-banking-for-small-business/#GUIDES)
